sentences.show: In under 100 days, a quiet Finnish farmer became, by most counts, the deadliest sniper in history.
His name was Simo Häyhä. Legend calls him the White Death.
He stood 5 foot 3, and grew up hunting in the forests on the Russian border.
In November 1939, the Soviet Union invaded Finland.
Häyhä was sent to Kollaa, where the cold fell to minus forty.
He dressed all in white. Most Soviet soldiers had no winter camouflage at all.
His rifle had iron sights. No scope.
He kept snow in his mouth, so his breath wouldn't show.
He went out before dawn, and came back after dark.
On one day in December, he is credited with 25 kills.
The army confirmed 259 with his rifle.
His secret memoir, found in 2017, says around five hundred. He called it his sin list.
Some historians doubt it, and say just over two hundred.
On 6 March 1940, an explosive bullet tore through his face.
They thought he was dead, and laid him on a pile of bodies.
Then someone saw his foot move.
He woke up a week later, on the day the war ended.
Then he read about his own death in the paper, and wrote in to correct it.
He lived to 96. Asked how he got so good, he said one word. Practice.
Simo rarely missed. Don't miss the next story. Subscribe.
